sectionDek: Short editorial briefs tied to our calculators. Not live wire copy and not affiliated with NerdWallet.

items.title: Mortgage rate board, Nov 26: planning averages ease a touch
items.dek: Our editorial U.S. 30-year planning average sits near 6.28%. Run your payment before you chase a quote.
items.author: aFinanceCalculator Editorial
body: aFinanceCalculator keeps an editable editorial rate board in /data/market-rates.json. As of Nov 26, 2026, the U.S. 30-year fixed planning average is 6.28% and the 15-year average is 5.55%. These are benchmarks for modeling — not a lender lock.

If rates feel a little lower than last month’s desk notes, re-run principal and interest with your down payment and term. Taxes, insurance, and mortgage insurance are still outside the payment unless you add them.
Canada readers can swap to the 5-year fixed benchmark (about 4.49% in the same file) and use the Canada mortgage engine for semi-annual compounding.

items.title: Holiday spending 2026: set the budget before Black Friday hits
items.dek: Decide the number first. Then decide what is worth a swipe — and what can wait until January.
items.author: aFinanceCalculator Editorial
body: Big sale weekends reward people who already know their wants vs needs split. Use a simple 50/30/20 layout: needs, wants, and savings/debt — then park a holiday cap inside wants.
If you will carry a balance, model payoff months on the credit card engine before you stack 0% intro offers you cannot clear.
Skip list starter: gadgets you have not researched, extended warranties you do not understand, and ‘only today’ carts that blow next month’s rent buffer.

items.title: Four money moves before the next tech outage
items.dek: When apps freeze, cash, paper backups, and a paid-ahead bill matter more than another fintech tip.
items.author: aFinanceCalculator Editorial
body: Keep a small amount of physical cash for transit, food, and tips when tap-to-pay is down.
Screenshot or print the last statement for cards and loans you may need to reference offline.
Pay critical bills a day early when storms or known maintenance windows are announced.
Park the rest of your emergency fund in an FDIC/CDIC-aware HYSA and use the compound engine to see what a 3–6 month buffer earns at today’s editorial APY benchmarks.

items.title: Thanksgiving travel: gas prices vs the EV cost line
items.dek: Road-trip math is fuel, time, and depreciation — not just the pump screenshot on social media.
items.author: aFinanceCalculator Editorial
body: Holiday fuel headlines move week to week. Before you change plans, estimate trip gallons × local price, then compare that to home charging or public charging for an EV on the same miles.
Add parking, tolls, and the cost of an extra overnight if charging slows you down — time has a money cost too.
If you are financing a vehicle swap, pair this with the auto loan and auto refinance desks instead of judging on fuel alone.

items.title: Hotel points news is fun — payoff math still wins if you carry a balance
items.dek: Issuer perk updates make great headlines. Revolving APR usually beats any bonus night.
items.author: aFinanceCalculator Editorial
body: Loyalty program refreshes (new partners, milestone bonuses, transfer sweet spots) matter most when you pay the statement in full every month.
If you are revolving a balance, run months-to-debt-free at your APR before optimizing points. Interest often erases the value of the perk.
After the balance is gone, use utilization and budget tools to keep the card as a cash-flow instrument — not a high-APR loan.
